name: Bin Laden family

summary.text: The Saudi bin Laden family, owners of the Saudi Binladin Group construction company, were investors in the Carlyle Group's Carlyle Partners II fund, a commitment reported as about $2 million and dating from 1994. In late October 2001, after the September 11 attacks carried out under Osama bin Laden, whom the family has disavowed, Carlyle and the family severed the relationship, with Carlyle buying out the family's stake; a Carlyle executive said the decision was mutual and not a response to wrongdoing.

facts.claim: The New York Times, as relayed by News24, reported that the bin Laden family's commitment to Carlyle's Partners II fund dated to 1994, that much of the money was invested in later years, and that a Carlyle-linked source said Carlyle bought out the family's stake in October 2001.
facts.quote: Carlyle bought out the family's stake, and that a separate $20,000 investment was also being liquidated

facts.claim: A Carlyle executive said the October 2001 decision was not a response to wrongdoing; both sides felt the connection was drawing more attention than it deserved, after critics argued the family could profit from higher U.S. military spending.

openQuestions: Site claim tested: 'The Saudi bin Laden family had about $2 million in a Carlyle fund, severed by mutual agreement at the end of October 2001' — supported in substance; the $2 million figure appeared in this research only in Wikipedia and a CounterPunch piece (which said 'at least' $2 million) and is not recorded as a fact here. The site cites Aviation Week's $2.02 million figure, which was not opened.
The site's alias 'Saudi Binladin Group' treats the company and the family as one entity; the Saudi Binladin Group's own ownership and any Carlyle relationship were not researched.
No source was found connecting the bin Laden family's Carlyle stake to George H.W. Bush or James Baker beyond their separate roles at Carlyle.
